courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Through readings, discussion, and Native guest lecturers, introduction to fundamental concepts and history of federal Indian law and policy. courses.description: Tutorial, one hour; activity, three hours. Course 198A is enforced requisite to 198B, which is enforced requisite to 198C. Limited to senior honors program students. courses.title: Honors Research in American Indian Studies
courses.description: Tutorial, one hour; activity, three hours. Enforced requisite: course 198B. Limited to senior honors program students. Completion of honors thesis or comprehensive research project under direct supervision of faculty member. May be repeated for credit. Individual contract required. Letter grading.

courses.title: Individual Studies: Capstone Synthesis
courses.description: Tutorial, three hours. Preparation: successful completion of eight upper-division major courses. Limited to senior American Indian Studies majors. courses.title: Working in Tribal Communities: Introduction
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. courses.title: Working in Tribal Communities: Preparing for Fieldwork
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. courses.title: California Indian Strategies for Contemporary Challenges
courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Concurrently scheduled with course C230. Letter grading.

courses.title: California Indian History
courses.description: Lecture, four hours. Introduction to overview of California Indian history, specific tribal community histories, and/or contemporary California Indian history through readings, discussion, and Native guest lecturers. May be repeated for credit with topic change and consent of interdepartmental chair. Concurrently scheduled with course C270. Letter grading.

courses.title: Cultures of Native Southern California
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Introduction to Southern California indigenous societies through readings, discussion, guest lecturers, and direct community participation. courses.description: (Same as Sociology M161.) Lecture, three hours. Requisite: course M10 or Sociology 1. Comparative and historical study of political, economic, and cultural change in indigenous North American societies. Several theories of social change, applied to selected case studies. Letter grading.

courses.title: Field Methods in Cultural Anthropology
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Designed for juniors/seniors. Introduction to skills and tools of data ascertainment through fieldwork in cultural anthropology. Emphasis on techniques, methods, and concepts of ethnographical research and how basic observational information is systematized for presentation, analysis, and cross-cultural comparison. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Economic Anthropology
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Requisite: course 3. Introduction to anthropological perspectives for interpretation of economic life and institutions. courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Comparative analysis of role of environment, history, and culture in structuring of patterns of gender and sexuality. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour (when scheduled). Designed for juniors/seniors. Particular attention to subsistence systems and their relationship to social institutions and cultural practices, especially religion. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Ethnography of South America
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Introduction to ethnography of South American Indians, with special emphasis on Lowland South America. Survey of history and development of man and society in this world area and examination of exemplary cultures symptomatic of various levels of cultural achievement. P/NP or letter grading.

courses.title: Culture and Society
courses.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; fieldwork. Required as preparation for both bachelor’s degrees. courses.description: (Same as Gender Studies M154Q.) Lecture, three hours. Recommended preparation: prior anthropology or gender studies courses. Designed for junior/senior social sciences majors. Comparative study of women’s lives and gender systems and cultures from anthropological perspective. Critical review of relevant theoretical issues using ethnography, case study, and presentations. courses.description: Seminar, three hours. Requisites: three courses from 20 through 31. Critical examination of history of discipline of art history, with studies of various theoretical, critical, and methodological approaches to visual arts. Letter grading.

courses.title: Arts of Native North America

courses.title: Japanese American Experience
courses.description: Lecture, three hours. Not open to freshmen. Survey of immigration history, settlement patterns, and experiences of Japanese Americans. courses.title: Pilipino American Experience
